summary: Both segments are generally faithful, with fixed terms and abbreviations expanded as ruled. Faults: 'Rabbeinu Bachya' for בר' בחיי (Rabbi); Deut 17:8 and Lev 4:13 quoted with the wrong connective and verb form; נמנע glossed 'avoidable'; the Ps 119:69 allusion in 3:4 (טפלתם עלינו שקר זדים) misread as 'ascribed ... arrogant falsehood'; Midrash ha-Gadol not transliterated; the title אלצלאם transliterated as 'al-Salam' against its spelling; and several token glosses, notes and apparatus lines. ב"ד, שגגו and ברמות רוחא were checked: ב"ד is raised for the owner, שגגו and ברמות רוחא stand.

patches.value: 4) The authority of our rabbis, the masters of the new Kabbalah, shall not be greater than the authority of the Great Beit Din who sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, and their grasp is no greater than the grasp of the Great Sanhedrin! And yet the Torah said that if they erred and ruled to permit the forbidden, or sinned inadvertently in idolatry, etc. We have learned from the Torah and from our rabbis, in the tractate Horayot, that the Great Beit Din can err and rule a permission in some particular case of idolatry. For man is formed of clay, whether great or small, and is prone to err; therefore the Torah commanded: "If a matter is too hard for you in judgment, etc. and you shall arise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose," in order to lessen the error. How is it not impossible that even the Great Beit Din should not err. For it is said in the Torah, "and a matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly. And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation it was done in error." And according to the shortness of our understanding, when we see the great difference between our early rabbis, and how was their faith in the matter of divinity and the unity of the Name, may He be blessed, according to the holy Torah, as explained by Rabbi Bachya, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, and Rabbi Yehuda Halevi in the Kuzari and in his prayers, and Rabbi Saadia Gaon in the Emunot ve-De'ot, and the Rambam in his work, and in his commentary on the Mishnah, and in the Moreh Nevukhim. And the Roke'ach in the Gate of Unity, and the Sefer Mitzvot Gadol, and Rabbi Yosef Albo in the Sefer ha-Ikkarim, and Rabbi Meir Aldabi in the Shevilei Emunah. And many others, and likewise the complete ones. And how is it now in the books of our later rabbis, according to the new Kabbalah, which is drawn on from the start of the sixth millennium with cords of falsehood until it became in our time as with cart-ropes, and they believed in many gods. And that the principal point in them, to which all our worship and blessings are directed, is the last partzuf in Emanation, called (quick to anger) Ze'ir Anpin.
patches.reason: Four faults. (1) 'Rabbeinu Bachya': the Hebrew is בר' בחיי, i.e. ב + ר' (Rabbi); the fixed 'Rabbeinu Bachya' is for the written רבינו בחיי, so 'Rabbeinu' adds a word; the author of Chovot ha-Levavot is named 'Rabbi Bachya'. (2) Deut 17:8 continues 'וקמת ועלית': 'Then arise' replaces 'and' by 'then' and turns the perfect with vav into an imperative; the verse's form is 'and you shall arise and go up'. There is no full stop after וכו' here. (3) Lev 4:13 'ונעלם דבר מעיני הקהל': דבר has no article, and ונעלם is a vav-consecutive perfect after the conditional, so 'a matter is hidden', not 'the matter was hidden'. (4) 'איך אינו נמנע שלא יטעו': נמנע is 'impossible', so the clause is 'impossible that they not err'; the English keeps the sense but the gloss 'avoidable' is wrong and the double negative is lost. Style: 'runs' loses the pull of הנמשכת, which echoes משכי in Isa 5:18 (the same verse as the cords); 'is drawn on' keeps it. 'Shevilei' is the spelling the rulings use.

patches.reason: נמנע is 'impossible' (that which is prevented), not 'avoidable'; with שלא יטעו the clause means 'impossible that they not err', i.e. they must err.

patches.value: שגגו: from שגגה, an inadvertent act (cf. Num 15:24 לשגגה); distinct from טעו, 'erred' in ruling; 'sinned inadvertently' stands
patches.reason: Checked: 'sinned inadvertently' is acceptable, because שגגה is the term of the Torah for an unwitting transgression (Lev 4:13, Num 15:22-29); a note records the distinction from טעו.

patches.value: ב"ד = בית דין, a court of law; kept as 'Beit Din' (see question)
patches.reason: Rulings are silent on ב"ד. 'Beit Din' is left untranslated (the glosses expand the abbreviation, so every word is accounted for). The rulings translate ordinary Hebrew and transliterate only titles and fixed terms, so the proposed ruling is: ב"ד / בית דין = 'court'; ב"ד הגדול = 'the Great Court' (as the English already renders לשכת הגזית and סנהדרין גדולה). If the owner prefers the transliteration, it stands and should be fixed for the work.

value: ולא יהא כח ... גדול מכח: a negated future (יהא) with a comparison; the English keeps the repeated 'the authority of' so that the comparison is plain.

איך אינו נמנע שלא יטעו: נמנע is 'impossible', so the clause says that it is impossible for even the Great Beit Din not to err, that is, error is unavoidable; the full stop of the Hebrew is kept and the English keeps 'How is it not ...'.
Three Torah passages are cited: Deut 17:8 (quoted, with וכו' as the author's truncation sign), Lev 4:13 and Num 15:24 (introduced by שהרי נאמר בתורה and continued by והיה).

The long period ולפי קוצר דעתינו ... is divided at 'when we see' and 'how was their faith'; no clause is dropped and the order of the list of authors is kept. It has no main clause of its own: the main clause is ואמונה זו החדשה רחוקה מאד in 3:4.
patches.reason: Corrects the note on נמנע and says where the period's main clause is.

value: Base text: Wikisource; not yet collated with the 1931 scan (open question 2), so the English is the base text as it stands.
Printed list marker ד) (the fourth item) opens the paragraph; the next paragraph opens ה) (the fifth item).
Deut 17:8, quoted with 'etc.' marking the author's omission (וכו').
Lev 4:13, quoted: ונעלם דבר מעיני הקהל.
Num 15:24, quoted: והיה אם מעיני העדה נעשתה לשגגה.
Isa 5:18, embedded allusion (no quotation marks): בחבלי השוא and כעבות העגלה; הנמשכת echoes משכי in the same verse.
Prov 14:17, for the author's קצר אפים, set against ארך אפים in Exod 34:6.
Job 33:6, embedded allusion (no quotation marks): קורץ מחומר echoes מחמר קרצתי, 'formed from clay'.
patches.reason: Verse allusion not listed: קורץ מחומר (Job 33:6); and the echo of Isa 5:18 in הנמשכת.

patches.value: Plain sentences follow the Hebrew full stops. The Torah quotations take double quotation marks; the author's וכו' is kept as 'etc.'. The list of authors is elliptical in the Hebrew after the full stop at הנבוכים, and the English keeps that ellipsis. The period that begins ולפי קוצר דעתינו has no main clause here; 3:4 supplies it.
patches.reason: The English keeps the Hebrew full stops, so the segment from 'And the Roke'ach ...' to the end is a run of sentence fragments, against the checklist ('every sentence has a main clause'). The Hebrew period itself has no main clause (it is completed by 3:4, ואמונה זו החדשה רחוקה מאד). Proposed ruling: where a Hebrew period has no main clause and the next segment supplies it, keep the Hebrew full stops, as now, and record it in the note; or, if the owner prefers sentences, join the fragments with semicolons from 'And how was their faith' to the end and close the segment with a dash. The current English is faithful and stands until the owner rules.

patches.value: 5) And this new faith is very far from the way of our holy Torah, written and oral. Therefore we separated ourselves from it, and we clung to the words of our rabbis of blessed memory, the masters of the Mishnah and the Talmud, Bavli and Yerushalmi, and the decisors, and the midrashim of our famous rabbis, Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma and Yalkut Shimoni, and Midrash ha-Gadol found in Yemen in manuscript, and Nur al-Tzalam, and the like. Also, the remnant of the books of our forebears, the sages of Yemen, we find and see that they adhere to the words of the great ones mentioned above and to their opinions. And when you saw that we separated from the new Kabbalah, your anger burned against us, and in haughtiness of spirit you, the arrogant, smeared falsehood on us. And we asked you to teach us the way: how would the words of our rabbis, the new Kabbalists, agree with the words of our early rabbis mentioned above, and with the words of the Tannaim and the Amoraim. And your answer to us was in the manner of deception and taunts.
patches.reason: (1) Ps 119:69, 'טפלו עלי שקר זדים' ('the arrogant smear me with falsehood'), is the model of 'וברמות רוחא טפלתם עלינו שקר זדים': the verse's wording governs. טפל עליו שקר is 'to smear falsehood on someone', not 'ascribe'; עלינו is 'on us'; and זדים (plural) is not an adjective of the singular שקר but the noun 'the arrogant', here those addressed. 'Arrogant falsehood' is wrong. (2) Midrash ha-Gadol is a book title, which the rulings transliterate. (3) The Arabic title אלצלאם is written with צ; Arabic 'salam' (peace) would be written with ס; the rulings say to transliterate a Judeo-Arabic title as the place writes it. 'Light of peace' was an unsupported guess (see the question on token 3:4.41). (4) כראותכם with the perfect חרה in the main clause is 'when you saw', not 'as you see'. (5) קינטורים is 'taunts, provocations' (קנטר), not 'quarrels'.

patches.value: אלצלאם as printed: the צ stands for Arabic ص or ظ; 'al-Salam' (السلام, peace) would be spelled with ס. If the Arabic is الظلام, the title is Nur al-Zulam, 'Light of the Darkness' (Hebrew title Me'or ha-Afelah)
patches.reason: Proposed ruling, following the pilot ruling on printed words that echo a likelier one: translate the printed word, record the likelier one in the token note and apparatus. I am fairly but not entirely certain of the identification; the owner should decide whether to name the likely title in the English.

value: The paragraph is a chain of first-person plural past acts (פירשנו, ודבקנו, שאלנו); the reply of the other side is in the perfect (והיתה).
ושאלנו אתכם ... איך יסכימו: the question is indirect (איך with the imperfect); the English keeps it as a report, 'how would ... agree'.
וכראותכם ... חרה אפכם: כראותכם is the infinitive with כ, 'upon your seeing'; the tense comes from the main verb חרה, hence 'when you saw'.

וברמות רוחא טפלתם עלינו שקר זדים: the Aramaic idiom ברמות רוחא is translated by its sense; the rest adapts Ps 119:69 (טפלו עלי שקר זדים), in which זדים, 'the arrogant', is the subject; here it names those addressed.
patches.reason: The old note said the indirect question 'carries a full stop' (it does not) and did not recognise Ps 119:69.

value: Ps 119:69, embedded allusion (no quotation marks): טפלו עלי שקר זדים, adapted to טפלתם עלינו שקר זדים.
Printed אלצלאם (3:4.41), transliterated as written 'al-Tzalam'; the likelier title is Nur al-Zulam, 'Light of the Darkness' (Hebrew Me'or ha-Afelah); 'al-Salam' would be spelled with ס.
patches.reason: Allusion not listed; likelier title for the printed spelling recorded (pilot ruling on printed words).

value: Midrash ha-Gadol: a midrashic compilation on the Torah, preserved above all in Yemenite manuscripts; the author names it as 'found in Yemen in manuscript'.
patches.reason: A book the reader needs identified; stated at the level the Hebrew gives.
